resources.string: SpeakerLink needs the \"Nearby devices\" permission to find, pair and connect your speakers and headphones. It never uses it to work out your location, and the app has no internet access.
On this Android version, finding Bluetooth devices requires the location permission. SpeakerLink never uses your location, and the app has no internet access.
Turn on Bluetooth to see and connect your speakers and headphones.
Up to %1$d Bluetooth audio devices can be connected at once.
No Bluetooth device is playing right now
Android plays on one Bluetooth device at a time. The Together tab shows ways to hear it on several.
No paired speakers or headphones yet. Tap Scan and put your device in pairing mode.
Searching for devices in pairing mode…
Put your speaker or headphones in pairing mode (usually by holding the Bluetooth or power button until a light blinks), then tap Scan.
Also nearby, but not in pairing mode: %1$s
Couldn\'t reach the speaker\'s control service.
This speaker doesn\'t offer the JBL control service.
The speaker didn\'t answer. Close the JBL app on other phones and try again.
The Nearby devices permission is missing.
The speaker answered but did not report its battery.
Battery and info use JBL\'s unofficial control protocol and may not work on every model.
Pick the model if SpeakerLink got it wrong, for example after the speaker was renamed.
Up to %1$d speakers in one group
Play the same audio on several speakers or headphones. Depending on your phone, it can play on two devices at once itself, and many speakers can link up with each other.
Pair your speakers or headphones on the Devices tab first.
Select at least two devices to see how this phone can play on them together.

Many speakers can link up with each other, usually within the same brand: with a party or stereo button, or in the maker\'s app. Connect your phone to one of them and link the rest to it. They all play what your phone plays.
JBL speakers: your phone streams to one speaker, the host, and the others get the music from it over PartyBoost, Auracast or Connect+. Speakers of different link systems can\'t be in the same group.
Switch every speaker on and put them close together.
Connect your phone to %1$s. Only the host needs a Bluetooth connection to the phone.
Within about 30 seconds, press the %1$s button on %2$s.
Start TWS pairing on %1$s as described in its manual.
Open JBL\'s PartyBox app and link %1$s with %2$s in Party mode.
These two speakers can also play as a stereo pair (left and right) instead of Party mode, set in JBL\'s app.
All speakers play the same music (Party mode). Stereo needs exactly two speakers of the same model.
Play music on your phone. Every speaker in the group plays it.
The Charge 3 uses JBL Connect on its original firmware and Connect+ after its firmware update, so it links with only one of the two generations.
A speaker here supports two link systems (Xtreme 4, PartyBox Club 120 or Stage 320). It was put in this group and can be in only one group at a time.
Newer PartyBoxes get Auracast and linking with other speakers through firmware updates in JBL\'s PartyBox app.
Linking support of at least one model here is not confirmed.
These speakers use different link systems, so they can\'t all play in one group.
JBL speakers that can\'t join a group
Unknown model. Set the model in the speaker\'s menu on the Devices tab.
It\'s unclear whether this model can link with other speakers.
This model can\'t link with other speakers.
Other speakers use %1$s too, but this model links only with certain models. See the list on the Info tab.
The %1$s group is full (at most %2$d speakers).
Tip: play the test sound. Every linked speaker should chime.
This Galaxy phone can play on two Bluetooth audio devices at once: two speakers, two headphones or one of each. Connect both, open the media output panel and select both.

This phone can share its audio with up to two LE Audio headphones or speakers that support Auracast. Other devices play one at a time: keep them connected and switch with Play here on the Devices tab.
This phone plays on one Bluetooth audio device at a time. Keep several connected and switch between them with Play here on the Devices tab, or use speakers that link up themselves (below).

SpeakerLink connects your Bluetooth speakers and headphones, shows which one is playing and switches between them with one tap. The Together tab shows how to hear the same audio on several devices at once. JBL speakers get extras: model, battery and firmware, a locate sound and step-by-step linking.

SpeakerLink is an independent open-source app. It is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by JBL or HARMAN International. JBL, PartyBoost and Connect+ are trademarks of HARMAN International Industries, Incorporated. Auracast is a trademark of the Bluetooth SIG.
SpeakerLink has no internet permission, no ads and no tracking. Everything stays on your phone.
